speakingObjectives: Chat with a fellow guest: say what you eat for breakfast, for example 'Je mange des chilaquiles au petit-déjeuner.'
Ask whether they drink coffee or tea: 'Vous buvez du café ou du thé ?'
Ask whether they live here: 'Vous habitez ici ?'
Use vous with a guest you have just met, and switch to tu only if they suggest it.
sourceNotes: Passage title corrected from the prior draft: 'Desayuno en Oaxaca' is rendered as 'Petit-déjeuner à Oaxaca'. The Lyon and Grenoble settings were removed and the Oaxaca and Puebla setting restored.
Lucía is kept as the source name; 'Lucie' from the prior draft was corrected.

The Reader French is aligned line by line with the source English. Prior-draft mismatches were corrected: 'pain perdu' to chilaquiles, 'fruits' and 'salade de fruits' to frijoles and salsa verde, 'porridge' to avena, and 'lait' and 'fruit' lines to source meanings.
Named Mexican foods are kept as transliterated Spanish names: chilaquiles, salsa verde, huevos estrellados, frijoles, tocino, aguacate and avena.
The source tú register for a fellow guest is rendered with vous, since the guests have just met and polite fr-FR is required. This is noted as a register choice, not a grammatical equivalence.

Forms are limited to regular -er verbs present in the Reader (manger, habiter) to follow the source focus on regular present-tense endings. Lines 2 and 5 are not used as forms because they contain irregular prendre or boire.
The source -ir verb vivir has no regular -ir French equivalent in this lesson; habiter is used instead.
Reader line 2 and card 11 use prendre, and card 12 uses boire. These are irregular and appear only as lesson vocabulary, not as the focus forms.
residuals: Unreviewed draft: no qualified approval, no audio, and no claim of learner readiness.
No regular -ir French verb is present in the Reader, so the source -ir grammar point is not fully covered.
Irregular verbs prendre, boire, mettre and ouvrir appear in the card and Reader text. A French-speaking reviewer should check whether they fit this beginner pacing.

Spanish food names (chilaquiles, huevos estrellados, frijoles, tocino, avena, salsa verde, aguacate) have not been checked for French-speaking readers. A native reviewer should confirm the French rendering.
The vous register differs from the source tú and should be confirmed against the lesson's pedagogical intent.
No French-speaking Mexico variant with local currency or regional menus has been prepared.
